stories.summary: Jasmine Jasudavicius stated her case as a contender in the UFC women's featherweight division, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas to win by unanimous decision.
stories.body:
Instability and opportunity permeate the UFC women's flyweight division, which crowned a new champion two weeks ago and has a former two-time champ lurking in the wings while healing from injury. Several other title hopefuls have been jostling to position themselves to go for the gold.

Jasmine Jasudavicius seized the opportunity to make her presence felt among the leading contenders Saturday, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas in a clash of top-10 125-pounders to win by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night in Edmonton, Alberta.

The fight was the co-main event of a card headlined by Mike Malott's explosive knockout win over Joaquin Buckley. Malott, who like Jasudavicius is from Ontario and had the crowd firmly behind him, landed a knee to the chin that crumbled Buckley, who is No. 8 in the ESPN welterweight rankings and lost his third in a row.

"Hey, guys, I might be soft-spoken," Malott said afterward, "but I'm f---ing hard-hitting."

Malott's knockout came at 2 minutes, 32 seconds of the second round and put a ferocious cap on an event that tied a UFC record with 12 finishes (seven knockouts, five submissions). The other modern-era fight card with a dozen finishes was UFC Fight Night in Belgrade, Serbia, on Aug. 1.

Nevertheless, it was the night's lone bout to go the distance that had the highest stakes. Jasudavicius, No. 8 in the ESPN women's flyweight rankings, pulled off the upset against third-ranked Blanchfield, who came in situated behind only injured former champion Valentina Shevchenko and new titlist Natalia Silva. Blanchfield is also No. 9 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound top 10.

Jasudavicius (16-4) surely elevated her standing in the 125-pound hierarchy with a robust performance that produced her second straight victory.

Both women came in touted as elite grapplers, and Jasudavicius proved to be a step ahead by repeatedly taking the fight to the ground (five takedowns) and threatening submissions from dominant positions for long stretches of the first two rounds.

"I love grappling," she said. "I understand it. I'm pretty good at it. And I like to show what I've got."

Jasudavicius showed enough to impress the judges, getting the nod on all three scorecards (29-28, 29-28, 29-28). The announcement of the verdict drew a roar from the crowd, which was enthusiastically behind the 37-year-old competing in her home country.

"To be able to fight in Canada, you hear the crowd, man. We're about it," Jasudavicius said.

Jasudavicius and Malott were among a dozen Canadian fighters on the card who went a combined 5-7.

Jasudavicius' victory might not put her in position for an immediate title shot, but she has her sights on a future meeting with the new champion, who defeated her by decision in 2022 in her second UFC fight.

"I want to cross paths with Natalia Silva again," Jasudavicius said. "We had a little bit of history before, so it would be an epic story."

For Blanchfield (14-3), the defeat halted a two-fight winning streak. She outlanded Jasudavicius 62-43 in significant strikes, but the author of five UFC submissions never could get her ground game going. Jasudavicius put Blanchfield on the defensive the whole fight with nearly eight minutes of control time.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi scores twice, takes season tally to 25 in Miami win at Atlanta
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored two scintillating second-half solo goals to take his MLS-leading tally to 25 as Inter Miami brushed aside hosts Atlanta United 3-1 on Saturday.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi scored two trademark second-half solo goals to take his MLS-leading tally to 25 as Inter Miami brushed aside hosts Atlanta United 3-1 on Saturday.

After Mexico striker Germán Berterame put Miami ahead in the 45th minute, Messi took center stage after the restart with two goals in four minutes.

The first, in the 56th minute, came after Messi drove infield from the right wing and exchanged passes with Berterame on the edge off the penalty area before dancing past a desperate Atlanta defender and firing low into the net.

His second was more of the same. This time, Luis Suárez sent him free on a breakaway and the Argentine forward again bewitched a hapless defender before once more beating Atlanta goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos with his left foot.

Atlanta got a late consolation goal through a penalty from former Miami forward Fafà Picault.

"He never ceases to amaze the world," Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González said of Messi afterward. "I mean, I honestly can't believe that a guy like him, at 39 years old, is doing what he's doing. And what makes me happiest is seeing that he's truly happy. Because he's happy, he gives everything he has. He enjoys himself and feels right at home.

"As I always say, he pushes us to be better every single day. It's an immense joy to have him here. Everyone knows how special our relationship is. Every time I see him, he brings a smile to my face. I'm still constantly amazed by him."

At full time of Saturday's game, Messi had a six-goal lead in the race for MLS' Golden Boot and also had the joint-most assists (15), along with LAFC's Son Heung-Min, having been credited with a secondary assist on Berterame's opener.

Messi is the first player in MLS history to register 15 assists in three consecutive seasons. He now has a goal contribution in 13 straight matches, tying his second-longest streak with club and country in his career.

Saturday's brace also took Messi to 936 career goals, and his coach has no doubts that he can reach the 1,000 milestone.

"Yes, I believe he'll reach 1,000 goals," González said. "I have faith in that. I know he will, because he loves a challenge, he sets challenges for himself and since he's already achieved everything else, this will be no exception."

He added: "He dazzles me with every single action, every time I see him in training. I truly hope he continues to amaze us right up until the day he decides to retire, which, hopefully, won't be for a long time yet."

Messi's performance Saturday gave the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner another fond memory at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The game marked Messi's first visit there since the 2026 World Cup semifinal in July, when he provided two late assists to propel Argentina to a dramatic win over England.

Messi has four goals in three games since he bid farewell to the Argentina national team in a friendly against Benin earlier this month.

Miami, which clinched a spot in the playoffs Wednesday, has won three straight games and is second in the Eastern Conference behind runaway leader Nashville.

Atlanta, under Gerardo "Tata" Martino, Messi's former coach with Miami and Argentina, is languishing in the 14th spot in the Eastern Conference and facing an uphill battle to make the postseason.

Miami will return to action with a visit to the New York Red Bulls next Saturday.

ESPN's Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report.

stories.headline: RLWC: What we learned from the opening round
stories.summary: Australia survived an opening-night scare, Tonga delivered a historic victory and Samoa wasted little time showcasing their attacking firepower. Isaac Issa takes a look atthe opening weekend of action.
stories.body:
Australia survived an opening-night scare, Tonga delivered a historic victory and Samoa wasted little time showcasing their attacking firepower.

The opening round of the 2026 Rugby League World Cup provided an early look at the contenders, while leaving England facing a difficult path to the knockout stages.

Here are the biggest takeaways from Week 1.

Australia win, but leave room for encouragement for their rivals

Australia banked the result they needed against New Zealand, but their 24-22 victory offered plenty for their rivals to work with.

The Kiwis gained close to 300 more running metres than the Kangaroos, exposing an area Australia will need to address as the tournament progresses. Winning a tight contest is valuable; consistently conceding that much ground is a difficult way to defend a World Cup.

Jack Bostock's debut hat trick proved decisive, while Reece Walsh's long-range try underlined Australia's ability to turn a game through individual brilliance. Those threats remain even when the Kangaroos are struggling to establish control.

For New Zealand, the frustration is that a strong performance went unrewarded. Kalyn Ponga's two tries demonstrated what he can add to their attack, although the arm injury that ended his night and left him needing surgery, raises concerns.

Australia emerged with the points. New Zealand showed enough to suggest another meeting would be far from straightforward.

Tonga's defence gives their title challenge substance

Tonga's attacking talent attracts attention, but their defensive resolve was the most significant feature of their 30-12 victory over England.

Repeatedly challenged in the opening half, Kristian Woolf's side held England scoreless and reached the break ahead 10-0. When AJ Brimson's try narrowed the gap, Tonga responded with consecutive tries to regain control.

Haumole Olakau'atu finished with a double as Tonga recorded their first victory over England.

The result strengthens their position in the race for a semifinal berth, but the manner of the performance should be just as encouraging.

Tonga demonstrated they could absorb pressure, withstand a shift in momentum and take their opportunities. Those qualities will become increasingly valuable when the tournament reaches its decisive matches.

Their ability with the ball was already apparent. Holding England out through that opening period provided a stronger indication of how difficult they could be to beat.

England already have little margin for error

One defeat has left England facing the prospect of an early exit, even if they win both remaining pool matches.

Only two teams from the combined Pool B and C standings advance to the semifinals. Tonga now hold the head-to-head advantage over England, while Samoa's 78-4 win over France has established a substantial points-difference buffer.

England still have France and Papua New Guinea to play. Winning those fixtures is the immediate requirement, but the size of those victories could also become crucial.

That creates a difficult balance: chasing points while correcting the errors that undermined their opener.

England generated opportunities against Tonga, yet too often failed to turn them into scoreboard pressure. Against opposition capable of punishing those missed chances, promising passages were insufficient.

Their next two performances must deliver considerably more. Even then, qualification could depend on results elsewhere.

Fa'alogo highlights Samoa's enviable attacking depth

Sua Fa'alogo began Samoa's World Cup opener on the bench. He finished it with four tries and 252 running metres.

Introduced after Deine Mariner suffered a hamstring injury, the Melbourne speedster immediately demonstrated the value of Samoa's attacking depth in their 78-4 win over France.

With Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow starting at fullback, Samoa could still call upon another explosive runner capable of transforming an opportunity into points. Fa'alogo's performance gives coach Ben Gardiner plenty to consider as the opposition becomes stronger.

There was encouragement beyond the established names, too. Test debutant Francis Manuleleua ran for 223 metres, including 89 after contact, while Jermaine McEwen topped Samoa's tackle count.

France offered limited resistance, so the result alone cannot establish where Samoa sit among the leading contenders.

It did, however, show how many attacking options they possess, and how difficult selection could become if their emerging players continue to contribute alongside their stars.

stories.headline: Bears' Kyler Gordon returns with vengeance, answers critics
stories.summary: In his season debut, Gordon was a huge factor in Chicago's win Sunday after battling through various injuries.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- The ink was barely dry on the Chicago Bears' initial 53-man roster when general manager Ryan Poles cast doubt on whether nickel corner Kyler Gordon would ever play another down of football in Chicago.

"I don't know," Poles said on Sept. 1, before adding he still had hope.

Those three words spoke loudest about a frustrating situation inside Halas Hall. The Bears had planned for Gordon to become a cornerstone in Dennis Allen's defense. But he didn't participate in any team drills during the 2026 offseason because of a right calf injury. He spent all of training camp on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list before being moved to reserve/PUP, which meant he would have to miss at least the first four games. He wasn't even in the building to start the season while rehabbing independently.

The best way to quell concerns -- at least in the short term -- about dependability was to return to the lineup and dominate, which he wasted little time doing Sunday in Atlanta. Gordon, who was activated Saturday, became the first Bears defensive back with three sacks in a game since Todd Bell in 1983 as Chicago held off the Falcons, 31-23. Gordon became the third Bears player since sacks became official in 1982 to record three sacks and two forced fumbles in a game.

Gordon had a lot to think about as he stood by himself during the anthem inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The highest-paid slot cornerback in the NFL -- $13.3 million per year after signing an extension on April 15, 2025 -- Gordon had played in just five of Chicago's previous 25 games (21%). And while his teammates kept the faith, the injuries created some doubt about his dependability.

"I mean, it is what it is," Gordon said. "I can't control what someone else says.

"But at the end of the day, I'm going out there and do my job and do (it to) my best ability and be the best player and the leader at my spot."

Gordon's talent was never doubted. He was Poles' first draft pick, No. 39 overall in 2022 out of Washington, and Poles rewarded him with the three-year, $40 million extension with $31.25 million guaranteed. His skills were on display Sunday, but Gordon has a bigger hurdle to clear: staying healthy.

No stranger to soft tissue injuries, Gordon has dealt with multiple hamstring, calf and groin ailments. He's also had a concussion and a fracture in his right hand.

"He was ready to play," Bears coach Ben Johnson said. "I talked with Kyler yesterday morning, and [said], 'Hey, I think we want to activate you. Are you ready to go?' And he said, 'Absolutely,' and he sure enough was. So, huge spark there for us on the defense.

"We've got to make sure that we keep him on that right track. We've tried to limit his role a little bit, just making sure he was in good football shape. But those snaps that he had were huge ones for us today."

Trying to find cause of Kyler Gordon's injuries

Two stints on injured reserve in 2025 prompted the Bears and Gordon to investigate the root of his health problems. Was it overtraining or undertraining? Was it the type of training he was doing on his own? Was an underlying injury issue to blame for what Poles classified in July as "a delay" in his recovery?

In the offseason, the team organized a virtual meeting, according to a source with direct knowledge of the call, with the team's decision-makers, trainers, strength and conditioning and other support staff, as well as with people Gordon had hired to work with away from Halas Hall. The purpose was to get all parties on the same page with a plan for Gordon's rehabilitation and offseason training.

But frustrations continued as Gordon showed up with a calf injury to offseason workouts in late May.

To fully understand the recurring soft-tissue ailments, the Bears then sent him to see a specialist, according to a source familiar with the request.

Gordon learned during the rehab process that the issue not just his calf, but "something wrong with the way the glute was firing that created a posterior chain issue," according to a source. That caused the calf to strain as well as the hamstring.

Unlike during the previous offseason, Gordon stayed in the Chicagoland area to rehab and train. He worked with Montel Fleming, known as "Dr. Moe," on body alignment and injury prevention. Fleming also works with other Bears players, from Jaylon Johnson to defensive back Cam Lewis and running back D'Andre Swift.

The Bears told Gordon's camp during the offseason that he could work with "your guy, come back when you're ready," a source with knowledge of the situation recalled. But those on both sides admit that building consensus on how to attack a delicate injury was, at times, frustrating. One issue for Chicago, per a team source, was that multiple players with severe injuries -- offensive tackle Ozzy Trapilo (torn patellar tendon), pass rusher Dayo Odeyingbo (torn Achilles) and linebacker Noah Sewell (torn Achilles) -- returned to the team and the field before Gordon.

Poles said on Sept. 1: "any time you have an injury and you're coming back from something there's discomfort that you have to push through and that's what it comes down to. So we haven't been able to get over that hump and we're not progressing as fast as we'd like."

But Gordon's injury was much more complicated than a calf strain, a source added.

That Gordon was away from the team -- front offices and coaching staffs typically prefer their players rehab injuries at the team facility -- was an additional layer to consider.

And the Bears' messaging about Gordon's injury was hard to ignore. In June, while citing Gordon's on-field impact as undeniable, Ben Johnson pointed out that "you can only develop trust (as a player) by being available." That seemingly applied public pressure on Gordon, as did Poles' "I don't know" comment. A source involved believes the team was attempting to "light a fire" under Gordon with those comments.

Asked Sunday if his team and the Bears' medical staff are on the same page as far as working with Fleming, Gordon said: "Think that'd be a question for Coach."

Gordon tried to find the positives in what he went through last season, when he played in just three regular-season games and both postseason contests.

"I've just never been through that before," he said. "So obviously just learning to have that delusional optimism and just use that.

"So it's been great. Learned a lot and now we're here. So God's great."

Kyler Gordon didn't say he was vindicated, or needed to be

If there was doubt outside the locker room, it wasn't shared by Gordon's teammates.

"My dog came back after all the talk, all the chatter, worked his ass off, came back and balled," Jaylon Johnson said.

When asked what it meant to have him back, defensive end Daniel Hardy said: "Everything, man. That guy came out here and put his heart and soul on tape. Phenomenal athlete.

"He was working his butt off trying to get back to us and y'all could see it out there. He wasn't just chilling at home. He was out there grinding and working and getting his body healthy so he could come back and be the star that he is."

Receiver Rome Odunze played with Gordon at Washington and still gets caught by surprise by his teammate.

"You think you've seen it all from that guy and then he goes out there and does some stuff like that," Odunze said. "He's one of those players that gets you up out of your seat for sure. The way he moves, his ability to impact the game is incredible.

"So, super glad to have him back."

A Bears defense that had allowed 6.2 yards per play (30th in NFL) and ranked 28th in explosive play rate allowed (7.6%) prior to his return Sunday believes Gordon could fix some of the unit's biggest vulnerabilities.

The Falcons entered the game averaging 361.8 yards per game and were held to 257. Gordon's impact off the nickel blitz was a major factor.

"Because he's the best in the league at it," Jaylon Johnson said.

For Hardy, Gordon's impact went beyond the box score.

"It's just the fact that our brother is back," Hardy said. "We've all spent a lot of time together and we're really close in that locker room.

"And to see him fight his way back onto the field, it was great to see."

As far as whether he felt vindicated in the face of doubt, Gordon chose to look ahead.

"That's just the nature of the world," he said. "I don't see everything. So I got a pretty close (group), so I don't really hear things unless people, my friends told me or something like that.

"But on to the next."

stories.headline: Barcelona's Eric García, Jules Koundé ruled out of PSG clash with injury
stories.summary: Eric García and Jules Koundé have both been ruled out of Barcelona's Champions League game against Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.
stories.body:
Eric García and Jules Koundé have both been ruled out of Barcelona's Champions League game against Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.

García will also miss Sunday's Clásico against Real Madrid after being ruled out for up to four weeks with a thigh injury picked up in Saturday's win at Real Betis.

Koundé will be assessed ahead of Madrid's visit to Spotify Camp Nou in LaLiga this weekend after spraining his ankle in the same game.

The loss of García and Koundé leaves Barça coach Hansi Flick without either of the players he has used at right-back this season.

However, João Cancelo and Xavi Espart, both used as left-backs this year, can play there, as could Alejandro Balde.

García's injury also leaves Barça short at centre-back, with Andreas Christensen currently out with a thigh issue, too.

That leaves Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín as the only available central defenders in the squad ahead of Tuesday's showdown with the European champions.

Midfielders Rodri and Frenkie de Jong have also played there in the past, with Flick confirming the Dutchman could be an option at the back after he returned to training last week.

- 'Best in the world' Yamal propels Barcelona to record-equaling LaLiga start

- Manuel Pellegrini bemoans 'inexplicable decisions' as Real Betis lose to Barcelona

- Yamal vs. Mbappé: Which Clásico star has stronger claim to win the Ballon d'Or?

Elsewhere, following De Jong's return to the matchday squad at the weekend, Barça are in good shape ahead of the biggest week of their season so far.

Captain Raphinha returned off the bench against Betis and will be available for Tuesday's game in Paris and Madrid's visit on Sunday.

Barça are seeking to maintain their perfect start to the season in France after winning all 11 of their matches in all competitions to date.

stories.headline: Ugonna Onyenso thought his NBA dream was over -- then the Detroit Pistons called his name
stories.summary: Detroit Pistons center Ugonna Onyenso was surprised to hear his name called out 53rd at the 2026 NBA Draft, having once believed his dream of making the league was over, but is now confident he can grow into the sizable shoes left by Isaiah Stewart.
stories.body:
Detroit Pistons center Ugonna Onyenso was surprised to hear his name called out 53rd at the 2026 NBA Draft, having once believed his dream of making the league was over, but is now confident he can grow into the sizable shoes left by Isaiah Stewart.

Stewart was traded to the Memphis Grizzlies in a deal which saw the Pistons acquire three future second round Draft picks. Onyenso, who bounced back at Virginia Cavaliers following spells at Kentucky and Kansas State, is a potential long-term successor -- though the 22-year-old from Owerri, Nigeria, knows there is a long journey ahead.

When asked what he wants the Pistons fans to remember him by, Onyenso told ESPN: "I feel like my defense -- what I bring on the floor defensively -- because they lost a shot-blocker and I want them to know that I'm going to bring that shot-blocking ability back on defense for them too."

Although he added that he even hopes to one day surpass Stewart in that aspect of the game, Onyenso admitted: "The pace is the biggest difference [between the NBA and college basketball]. My blocked shots have got to be on a different timing and I'm still figuring that out.

"Getting rebounds, getting pick-and-rolls really fast - the little things like that - being able to do it at a higher pace requires getting in shape and conditioning myself more, but I'm getting there."

Onyenso is also still adjusting to being a full-time professional basketball player as opposed to a student athlete, but he is certainly not complaining.

Having been developed through the NBA Academy Africa and then Putnam Science Academy in Connecticut, Onyenso arrived at Kentucky in 2022 as a highly-rated prospect with international experience for D'Tigers.

After a modest freshman year, Onyenso's sophomore season was derailed by a foot injury. He transferred to Kansas State, hoping to restore his spark, but the 2024-25 season was arguably the least productive of his college career.

After averaging 2.8 points, 2.4 rebounds and 0.9 blocks across 24 games, only two of which were starts, Onyenso feared his NBA dream was over.

Instead, a year with Virginia put him back on the map as he averaged 6.5 points and 4.9 rebounds per game and made the ACC All-Defensive team.

He said: "After Kansas State, I thought I had no shot to get into the NBA anymore. When I left Kansas State, I thought I was going to go to a low-major D1 [college], but as God may have it, I was fortunate enough to go to Virginia. That was when I [regained] hope that I may have a chance.

"When my coaches let me shoot the ball, I was like: 'Ok, I have a real chance to get back on the [Draft] board. It's all about being patient for me and locked into the goal. [If I had not made it to the NBA], I would have probably gone overseas and played."

As Draft night approached, Onyenso still was uncertain whether his career would continue in the NBA or abroad - and believed that if he was to get drafted, it would be as the last pick.

"I thought I was going to go undrafted or go 60th. The Bucks had already texted my agent, saying that if I was available at 60, they would pick me at 60," he recalled.

"I heard my name get called [53rd] and they didn't text my agent or nothing. I don't know if you saw - I didn't even have a reaction when my name got called."

Indeed, Onyenso was left shocked as he was drafted - nominally by the Houston Rockets, although his draft rights were initially traded to the New York Knicks, and he was then traded to the Pistons for cash considerations.

He has been working predominantly with Senegalese G League assistant coach Assane Sene - who has spent the preseason working with the Pistons big men.

Sene had previously received praise from Stewart for his impact, and has urged Onyenso not to put too much pressure on himself in his first year as he looks to fill the void left behind by the 25-year-old, but also to not get carried away if the NBA dream continues to go better than he had imagined it.

"Enjoy what you're doing first of all. Know why you are here and don't get too comfortable. Don't get too comfortable. When things start going your way, don't say: 'I'm not going in the gym tomorrow,'" Sene said on what Onyenso would have to do in order for his first year as a professional to be deemed a success.

"I feel like he's doing a really good job of not being too comfortable. He's very hungry and wants to keep getting better."

Sene and Onyenso have much in common, having both began their basketball journeys in Africa, gone on to play for Virginia, and struggled with injuries at different points in their basketball journeys.

Sene believes there are lessons for Onyenso in the journey of another homegrown African NBA player - Phoenix Suns center Khaman Maluach.

"[Khaman] Maluach - I remember watching him in college. From college to now, he's a completely different player, but he probably put the work in the gym and in the weight room. You need to fill up. You need to be a little stronger on the floor and be explosive before you can rebound the ball better," Sene said.

"Also, the NBA game is all about spacing. Maluach understands better the spacing - which Ugo has been doing a really good job [learning]. He's getting there, which is really fun to watch."

The Pistons will be in action against the Boston Celtics on Tuesday, Oct. 20, in the opening game of the NBA season at Little Caesars Arena.

The NBA is available to watch on ESPN Africa's DSTV channels 218 and 219 (ESPN 1 & 2), which for South African viewers are also available on Disney Plus.

stories.headline: ALCS Game 6: Lineups, live updates for Guardians-Rays
stories.summary: Tampa Bay is one win away from the Fall Classic as Cleveland battles to play another day -- and we've got it all covered.
stories.body:
It's win-or-go-home for the Cleveland Guardians in the American League Championship Series.

After the Tampa Bay Rays won two of three games in Cleveland to take a 3-2 series lead, they are just one victory away from punching their ticket to the World Series, where they would face the National League champion Milwaukee Brewers in a matchup of teams without a World Series title.

The ALCS moves back to Tampa Bay for Game 6 on Monday. Will the Rays keep rolling and advance to the Fall Classic for the first time in a full season since 2008? Or can the Guardians stave off elimination and force a decisive Game 7?

Stay tuned for lineups, game action and postgame analysis from Tropicana Field.

What the Rays need to do to win: Sit back and watch Fastball Freddy do his thing. As good as Drew Rasmussen has been lately, Peralta has been even better. His September/October will be remembered for a long time by Rays fans if he closes out the Guardians on Monday. His fastball has been that good. On offense, the Rays need to use the knowledge they've gained from seeing Cleveland's top relievers over the past couple of days. They're likely to get another dose of them in Game 6.

How the Guardians can stave off elimination: Cleveland has won already at Tropicana Park in this series, which has to give the team some confidence, considering it might be shaken after the last two days. It won't be easy on offense, but at least the Guardians are seeing Peralta for a third time -- and their at-bats got better as Game 5 wore on. stories.headline: Ranking the Premier League's best long-distance goals after Diego Gómez strike
stories.summary: Diego Gómez's long-range goal for Brighton vs. Palace was impressive, but which Premier League efforts are the best from history?
stories.body:
Diego Gómez added his name to an exclusive list of Premier League players who have scored goals from near the halfway line on Sunday afternoon, after walloping one in from long range in Brighton & Hove Albion's 5-0 demolition of Crystal Palace.

After receiving the ball in the center circle, the Paraguay international midfielder turned, spotted Palace keeper Walter Benítez off his line and proceeded to unleash a monstrous shot that sailed in from 55.7 yards.

That is the furthest out a goal has been scored in the Premier League since Wayne Rooney's similarly outrageous effort (63.4 yards) for Everton against West Ham United almost nine years ago.

Alongside Rooney, Gómez now joins some big names in the rundown of Premier League long-rangers. But how does his extraordinary strike against Palace stack up against the other raft of goals that have been scored around the halfway line?

14. Tim Howard (Everton) vs. Bolton Wanderers, 2012

The first of three goal-scoring keepers on the list, Howard successfully harnessed the power of the wind to score from inside his own area for Everton. While the distance was impressive, the goal loses several aesthetic points for being a freak, weather-assisted goal that bounced several times before hitting the back of the net.

13. Paul Robinson (Tottenham Hotspur) vs. Watford, 2007

Demonstrating his renowned set-piece mastery, Robinson scored for Spurs with a direct free kick from around 95 yards out when his aimless punt up field bounced high over the head of England rival Ben Foster and into the Watford goal.

12. Asmir Begović (Stoke City) vs. Southampton, 2013

The longest-distance goal in Premier League history (101 yards) was scored by Begović from inside his own penalty area with just 13 seconds of the game elapsed. The feat is certainly noteworthy, but the Bosnian was hugely assisted by a strong prevailing wind, a fortunate bounce, and the fact that his Saints counterpart, Artur Boruc, appeared to be playing in roller skates.

11. Xabi Alonso (Liverpool) vs. Newcastle United, 2006

After managing to evade an interfering referee, Alonso slung a speculative shot toward the Newcastle goal from the center circle that only really ended up in the back of the net thanks to the fact that goalkeeper Steve Harper's legs turned to jelly while trying to recover his position. Ingenious, but fairly low on style.

10. Stiliyan Petrov (Aston Villa) vs. Derby County, 2008

Villa thrashed Derby County 6-0 in what would prove to the latter club's Premier League annus horribilis, during which the Rams accrued a record low total of just 11 points. Petrov capped off the rout with a marvellously struck long-distance goal from the edge of the center circle.

9. Jonjo Shelvey (Swansea City) vs. Aston Villa, 2014

After bringing down an undercooked defensive clearance, Shelvey quickly assessed his options and chose to simply send the ball back from whence it came with an excellent long-range effort from the middle of the pitch.

8. Luis Suárez (Liverpool) vs. Norwich City, 2012

Suárez made a habit of terrorizing Norwich during his Liverpool days, but his longest-range goal against the Canaries came in 2012 when the Uruguay striker completed his hat trick from roughly 45 yards out.

7. Charlie Adam (Stoke City) vs. Chelsea, 2015

After the Stoke defense had quickly wrestled possession back from Chelsea, Adam was able to look up and launch a shot from midway inside his own half. Goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was able to get a flailing hand to the Scotland midfielder's effort, but couldn't prevent it from crossing the line.

6. Moisés Caicedo (Chelsea) vs Bournemouth, 2024

Scored on the final day of the 2023-24 season, Caicedo left it late to file his own entry for the Premier League goal of the season award with a 50-yard piledriver scored from the center spot. Unfortunately for the Chelsea midfielder, the actual award ended up going to Alejandro Garnacho for his overhead kick against Everton.

5. Wayne Rooney (Manchester United) vs West Ham United, 2014

Unusual in that it came from a bouncing ball, Rooney first demonstrated his ultra long-range prowess in 2014 when he dropped a spontaneous arching shot over bamboozled Hammers keeper Adrian from 45-plus yards out.

4. Maynor Figueroa (Wigan athletic) vs Stoke City, 2009

Reacting quickly to a free kick being given in his own half, Wigan full back Figueroa pounced on the opportunity to crack a 65-yard set piece soaring over the head of Stoke goalkeeper Thomas Sørensen in one fluid motion.

3. Wayne Rooney (Everton) vs West Ham United, 2017

A formidable and deceptively difficult first-time strike from Rooney that saw the ball sail with a perfect, flat trajectory over the head of stranded Hammers keeper Joe Hart, who had scurried out of his area to clear a loose ball.

2. Diego Gómez (Brighton & Hove Albion) vs Crystal Palace, 2026

It might not be the longest Premier League goal on record, but Gómez's ludicrous effort against Palace certainly ranks up there among the most technically adept. A beautifully flat, purposeful trajectory that rustled the net without bouncing. Bueno.

1. David Beckham (Manchester United) vs Wimbledon, 1996

The long-range Premier League strike by which all others are measured (literally, in some cases), Beckham's classic looping effort from the halfway line was famously achieved despite wearing someone else's boots on the very first day of the 1996-97 season and has since become the archetype of the genre.

stories.headline: Dylan Garand is living an NHL goalie's dream ... but will it last?
stories.summary: The 24-year-old has stepped into the spotlight due to injuries to Igor Shesterkin and Joonas Korpisalo. How long will his success last?
stories.body:
TARRYTOWN, NY -- Dylan Garand is living every goalie's NHL dream. Except he loathes how it started and he can't help but wonder how quickly it might end.

Garand, 24, spent his last four professional seasons as a goalie for the Hartford Wolf Pack, the AHL affiliate of the New York Rangers. That appeared to be his lot in life again for 2026-27, despite a promising training camp: The Rangers had star goalie Igor Shesterkin ready to play at least 65% of their games and veteran backup Joonas Korpisalo to fill in the blanks.

Before the season, the Rangers put Garand on waivers to be sent down to Hartford. While some expected he might be claimed by another team, Garand passed through and was demoted to the AHL. He got an apartment in the Hartford area and slept in a hotel for three nights while it remained unfurnished.

He never did get quality time in that new apartment. Korpisalo sustained a lower-body injury and was week-to-week. Garand was suddenly Shesterkin's backup for the Rangers' second game.

The Rangers' vibes early in the season were immaculate. After an opening night stumble against the Bruins, they won four straight games, looking like a team with playoff potential just nine months after GM Chris Drury set a letter to fans preparing them for a roster "retool."

Garand contributed to that early bliss with a 22-save shutout of Detroit in his first NHL start on Oct. 2 -- one night after Shesterkin became the talk of the sports world after scoring his first career goal in a win over Tampa Bay.

"On the ice, he's unreal to watch. He's my favorite goalie, honestly," Garand said of Shesterkin. "He was on another planet, playing so well. It really sucks what happened. I feel so bad for him."

The Rangers' season irrevocably changed on Oct. 9 when Shesterkin injured his right knee in the second period during a loss to the Washington Capitals. The next day it was announced that the Vezina-winning goalie would miss the rest of the season.

"It's awful. He's a pillar of this team. It stinks," captain J.T. Miller said at the time.

"It's obviously devastating. He's the best goalie in the world," forward Matt Rempe said.

Garand didn't initially know the severity of Shesterkin's injury. He saw him helped off the ice, but Garand's focus was on entering the game for the Rangers, stopping 10 of 11 shots he faced. "I did media the next day after practice and they were like, 'Oh, did you hear the news?' After we were done, I went and saw it was on TV," he recalled.

In an ideal world, Garand would have earned an NHL starting job through years of toiling in the AHL and patiently waiting for his chance. Instead, like so many backup goalies, his big break came at the expense of another goalie's broken body, getting unexpectedly thrust into the starter's crease.

"It's an unfortunate circumstance with Shesty, but now I'm just trying to help the team any way I can," Garand said.

In six appearances, Garand is 5-3-1 with a .927 save percentage and an impressive 1.82 goals-against average. His only previous NHL experience came last season, when he started three games and went 2-0-1, posting a fantastic .948 save percentage and a 1.62 goals-against average.

It's been a lightning-speed journey from apartment hunting in Hartford to starting goalie for the New York Rangers, under the glaring spotlights of Madison Square Garden.

"Yeah, it's obviously been crazy. But it's been a lot of fun," he said.

GARAND IS FROM Victoria, BC, and was drafted 103rd overall in 2020 by the Rangers from the Western Hockey League's Kamloops Blazers. His idol growing up was another BC native: Carey Price, who starred for 15 seasons with the Montreal Canadiens. Garand had Price's poster on his bedroom wall, but he didn't pattern his style after Price.

"As you get older, I think you just figure out what works for you. There are 64 goalies in the NHL and I don't think you can pinpoint two that play exactly alike," he said. "There are so many different ways to make saves. I just kind of stick to what works for me."

Kevin Woodley, a goaltending analyst for InGoal Magazine and NHL.com, said that Garand reminds him of Calgary Flames netminder Dustin Wolf.

"Exceptional edges and patience. He rarely gets too wide and low too soon, all of which fuels excellent movement and positioning," Woodley said.

If there's one aspect to Garand's game that's already caught coach Mike Sullivan's attention, it's his self assurance.

"He's got a lot of confidence in his game. He knows how important he is to helping this team win," Sullivan said. "He's trying to take advantage of the opportunity that he has."

Garand said he's just trying to live in the moment.

"Any opportunity that I get, I'm just trying to make the most of it and battle in there for the guys," he said. "I'm just trying to right now be present. It's really fun to play in the NHL. I definitely don't take it for granted."

Less fun for Garand: The speculation about how long his opportunity will actually last.

His locker room stall might as well be filled with ticking clocks:

Korpisalo will eventually return from injury -- he's been week-to-week -- and has 11 seasons and 334 NHL games to his credit. Tick, tick ...
ESPN's Emily Kaplan reported that recently retired goalie Jonathan Quick, 40, could be a possibility if the Rangers asked him to return. Quick was Shesterkin's backup for the last three seasons. Tick, tick ...
Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on "32 Thoughts" that Rangers goalie scout Scott Clemmensen recently took in a Buffalo Sabres game, reportedly to get a look at goalie Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen as a possible trade target. Tick, tick ...

Friedman's podcast dropped on Oct. 15. Perhaps coincidentally, or perhaps not, Garand had his worst NHL performance that night in a 7-1 loss at the rival New Jersey Devils. He gave up four goals on 13 shots and was pulled for the first time in his NHL career.

"Sometimes that happens. You don't really feel good about yourself," Garand said. "[But] the best goalies in the world -- Carey Price, Henrik Lundqvist, Igor -- everyone's been pulled. I wasn't happy. I didn't do a good enough job of being present. I let the self-doubt creep into my game too much."

On one day, Garand looked like the potential goaltending savior for the Rangers in what might have been a lost season without Shesterkin. On the next, he was chased from the crease, while his team's front office was checking on other options.

Because of that, Garand's next start, for many reasons, would be the most scrutinized of his short NHL career.

Garand returned to the crease on Saturday night against the Columbus Blue Jackets. The Rangers lost the game, 1-0 in overtime, but Garand made his statement: Stopping 28 of 29 shots, with a handful of highlight-reel saves.

"I thought that was a huge response from him. He's a high-character kid. The more you get to know him as a person, you knew he was going to bounce back," Sullivan said.

"I'm happy for him. He's a competitor and he wanted to be better," Miller said.

The Rangers captain said his team is prepared to support whoever is tending goal for the team -- but that Garand has impressed him.

"It doesn't matter who's in net for us. We have a job to do up front. We've talked about the void with Shesty out of the lineup, but Dylan's been unreal every time he's had a chance," he said.

Despite all those ticking clocks, Garand doesn't believe he has a limited amount of time to earn the Rangers' starting job this season.

"It's pro hockey. Anything can happen. All those decisions are out of my control. I just show up every day, focused on stopping pucks. And if they tell me to play, I'll play. If not, then I'm not. So that's just kind of my approach to it," he said. "I want to help this team win in any way I can."

And if he wins enough, Garand might even see about that breaking that apartment lease in Hartford.

"If I'm here for the whole year, then yeah, I'll try," he said. "But until I get permission to do that, I won't."

Formula 1 heads to Texas for the United States Grand Prix, with the championship battle set to heat up at the Circuit of the Americas.

Max Verstappen claimed his second victory this season after winning the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli continued to extend his lead in the title championship to 102 points from Mercedes teammate George Russell, and there is a mathematical chance he will be able to clinch the title in Austin.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the United States Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

It's a mix of fast corners, long straights and has one of the steepest elevation climbs to Turn 1.

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2012

Lap record: 1:36.169, Charles Leclerc (2019)

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Most wins: Lewis Hamilton with six (2007, 2012, 2014-2017) Other winners from the current grid are Verstappen (2021-2023, 2025) and Leclerc (2024).

Most poles: Hamilton (2007, 2016-2018) is tied with Michael Schumacher (2000-2002, 2006) on four. Other pole sitters from the current grid are Verstappen (2021 and 2025), Carlos Sainz (2022), Leclerc (2023) and Lando Norris (2024).

Weather forecast

The weather for the United States Grand Prix is expected to be light rain with a gentle breeze throughout the course of the weekend, with highs of 32°C.

What happened last time out?
Verstappen edged out Norris to take an imperious pole position by 0.291 seconds.

The Red Bull driver dominated the race and posed as a serious threat to McLaren's Norris and Oscar Piastri in the drivers' championship.

Norris finished second and cut his lead to 14 points to Piastri in the standings, who finished fifth. Verstappen ended the weekend only 40 points behind Piastri with five races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.

stories.summary: Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.
stories.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. -- - Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.

Griezmann has 12 goals and seven assists in 14 MLS appearances and is the first player in league history with a goal contribution in 12 of his first 14 career games.

Marco Pasalić scored a stoppage-time goal for Orlando (12-13-5). Maxime Crépeau had three saves.

Tai Baribo converted from the penalty spot in first-half stoppage time for D.C. (7-10-12).

Ojeda, just inside the top of the 18-yard box, chipped a first-touch pass over four defenders to a charging Griezmann on the give-and-go for a first-touch finish from 7 yards out to make it 1-0 in the 15th minute.

Ojeda flicked a back-heel volley, off a feed from Griezmann, past goalkeeper Sean Johnson and inside the left post to give Orlando a two-goal lead in the 22nd.

Griezmann intercepted a misplayed pass by Kye Rowles in D.C.'s defensive third, took two dribbles and rolled a shot into the net to make it 3-1 in the 50th minute.

Johnson finished with three saves.

Up next D.C.: Plays Wednesday at Cincinnati.

Orlando: Hosts New York City next Saturday.
